title: Prove exact Clifford Gram endpoints at every odd width
body:
**Enabling algebraic theorem:** two explicit degree-eight polynomials give the exact smallest and largest normalized four-qubit Clifford Gram eigenvalues at **every odd width `f >= 13`**. The extreme blocks swap with `f mod 8`. This replaces a fixed sufficient stability constant with the exact width-dependent coefficient-recovery contract. **No new kappa** or physical decoder is claimed.

Read the [all-width proof and two polynomials](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/9a8ce06644700ffa576d99316450bcb52835d6dc/research/clifford-odd-width-spectrum/PROOF.md), [complete spectrum and interval certificates](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/9a8ce06644700ffa576d99316450bcb52835d6dc/research/clifford-odd-width-spectrum/RESULT.json), [checker](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/9a8ce06644700ffa576d99316450bcb52835d6dc/research/clifford-odd-width-spectrum/verify.py), [source pins](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/9a8ce06644700ffa576d99316450bcb52835d6dc/research/clifford-odd-width-spectrum/SOURCE-PINS.json) and [credits](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/9a8ce06644700ffa576d99316450bcb52835d6dc/research/clifford-odd-width-spectrum/CREDITS.md).

Set `p=(f-1)/2`, `sigma=(-1)^floor((f+1)/4)` and `x=sigma*2^(-p)`. In the proof, `P` is the quotient row-one polynomial and `Q` is row two.

| Width modulo 8 | Exact minimum | Its eigenspace dimension | Exact maximum | Its eigenspace dimension |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 or 7 | `Q(x)` | 313,600 | `P(x)` | 256 |
| 3 or 5 | `P(x)` | 256 | `Q(x)` | 313,600 |

Every other irreducible block lies strictly between these endpoints. The Gram condition number is maximum/minimum; the normalized tensor-map condition number is its square root; the coefficient-recovery norm is the reciprocal square root of the minimum. The full alphabet attains each bound. Principal submatrices give valid bounds for every subalphabet, without a subset sharpness claim.

The complete 81-block spectrum is polynomial in `x`. There are 318 strict endpoint comparisons on the full intervals `[-1/64,0)` and `(0,1/128]`. Dividing each difference by a positive interval coordinate gives 2,544 strictly positive Bernstein coefficients. Two additional certificates prove positive minima. Exact coefficient expansion validates every certificate. This proves the infinite width range; the 35 finite width checks are corroboration. The condition numbers have sharp leading terms `1 + 408*2^(-p) + O(2^(-2p))` for the Gram and `1 + 204*2^(-p) + O(2^(-2p))` for the tensor map.

This extends [PR #7772](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7772)'s exact width-thirteen spectrum, head `1398fbdca3536389d8ac3c8b3aaa408f03e8f6c2`. It uses the phase and quotient framework from [PR #7766](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7766), head `d7c2dd1868c70f0addce2c0a4d3220149452f14b`. The actual phase is negative at widths 13/19 and positive at 15/17. A fixed negative sign would describe the wrong representation at half the odd widths.

Use Python 3.12 and the standard library:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/clifford-odd-width-spectrum
```

Both modes print this prefix and elapsed seconds:

```text
PASS_CLIFFORD_ODD_WIDTH_SPECTRUM 81 blocks 318 order proofs 2 positive endpoints
```

The unchanged threshold source checker runs. Both complete spectral moment identities hold coefficient by coefficient. Multiplicity integrality, dimensions and independent tuple-orbit norms pass at all odd widths 13–81. A literal 24-element one-qubit group checks all 576 products, 384 Pauli quotient fibres and four complete Gram spectra covering every odd residue modulo eight. Six altered-data/domain controls and the separate unsigned-phase control reject.

All 22 retained files are authenticated. Normal/optimized registered replay, syntax/indentation, committed bytes/source history/modes, export and sealed read-only Git-free serial replay pass. Hosted CI did not certify this package. The [plan job](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/44466577235/job/135365700006) failed in the shared `test_current_ci_section_matches_selected_record`: the base guide names frontier6030 while the selected record requires `make frontier7000-verify`. The log reports 760 tests, one failure and 24 skipped; package replay was skipped. This package changes no shared CI file. Local replay remains the scientific evidence.

Ali Romman (@aliromman) supplied the [threshold source](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/d7c2dd1868c70f0addce2c0a4d3220149452f14b/research/clifford-four-qubit-threshold/PROOF.md) and the [width-thirteen normalization and stability proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/1398fbdca3536389d8ac3c8b3aaa408f03e8f6c2/research/clifford-threshold-conditioning/PROOF.md). Nick Petalas (@petalas) supplied [PR #7747](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7747)'s [Sp(8,2) projection](https://github.com/petalas/integer-mult-bounds/blob/ff12ca358d601a21cd4b1f016b8a3a969ac44016/research/clifford-four-qubit-width-nine/PROJECTION.json). alephnan (@alephnan) supplied the [Pauli-sector and projective Gram framework](https://github.com/alephnan/integer-mult-bounds/blob/f7f32a18dde54e67624a9ed9cc7e1b266d9585c0/research/clifford-three-qubit-threshold/PROOF.md) in [PR #6714](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6714). The retained notices preserve the ATLAS, Thomas Breuer's CTblLib, MatShep and the earlier framework credit.

The published ordinary character table remains a mathematical input; its archive is not re-extracted here. No full four-qubit Gram matrix, full three-qubit or even-sector suite, selected cold replay, Lean or Docker run is supplied. Native preparation, inverse realization, precision allocation, routing, owned recovery, stock and complete caller costs remain unknown. Exact even-width endpoints are outside scope. No independent human or proof-kernel acceptance is claimed. `T(4)=13`, all five framework assumptions and the selected frontier remain unchanged.
